reason: The hypothesis transfers the laser-clad Inconel 718 transition layer concept from H13 steel (P8, P11) to a non-weldable nickel-based superalloy, combining it with the known hot-cracking problem in such alloys (P3, P6, P17). However, the transfer lacks a stated reason why it should work in this new material system, and the mechanism (thermal expansion matching, microstructural refinement) is taken directly from the H13 steel studies without adaptation or integration of superalloy-specific cracking mechanisms from the provided passages.
copied_elements: laser cladding of Inconel 718 transition layer (P8, P11)
Inconel 718 for thermal expansion matching and stress resistance (P8)
graded interface to alleviate stress concentration (P11)
hot cracking as a repair limitation for Ni-based superalloys (P3, P6, P17)
